typical_recipient: full professors
rule_text: IMU: 'A candidate's 40th birthday must not occur before January 1st of the year of the Congress at which the Fields Medals are awarded'.

typical_recipient: full professors (Fall: AIMS Senegal; Liu: Peking; Gupta: ISI Kolkata)
rule_text: Awarded to a researcher who is "less than 45 years of age on 31 December of the year of the award and has conducted outstanding research in developing countries".

typical_recipient: full professors (Hill, Hopkins, Ravenel 2022; Feyzbakhsh, Thomas 2025)
rule_text: AMS prize 'in recognition of a notable research memoir in geometry or topology published in the preceding six years'; the nominee must be an AMS member or the memoir published in a recognized North American journal; no age or career-stage cap.

typical_recipient: associate and full professors at research universities (one industry chief scientist)
rule_text: COPSS: the recipient must be under 41 throughout the award year, or under 46 with a terminal statistically related degree no more than 12 years old.

typical_recipient: postdocs, research instructors and junior faculty (Viazovska, Logunov, Peluse, Sahasrabudhe)
rule_text: IAS rules give "preference to nominees who received their PhD in the last ten years"; no age limit.

typical_recipient: full professors (Miller, Naber 2023; Dimitrov, Vicol 2025)
rule_text: Institut de Mathematiques de Toulouse prize rewarding 'research work in mathematics at the highest international level' in fields where Fermat contributed; no age, career-stage or recency restriction is stated (the separate Junior Fermat Prize is for undergraduates).

typical_recipient: full professors
rule_text: AMS: awarded every three years 'for a notable research work in analysis that has appeared during the past six years'; no age or career-stage restriction.

typical_recipient: full professors (Nelson: Aarhus; Newton: Oxford; Thorne: Cambridge; Merle, Raphael, Rodnianski, Szeftel)
rule_text: Recognizes "major breakthroughs in mathematical research"; each award cites a specific recent result; no age, career-stage or nationality restriction stated.

typical_recipient: full professors abroad (Sorek, Weizmann 2023; Williamson, Sydney 2024)
rule_text: 'The nominated individual must have gained her/his doctorate no more than 15 years ago', must have lived and worked outside Germany for more than five years and hold no permanent German post.

typical_recipient: assistant professors (Toronto, NYU, Penn in 2023)
rule_text: Rollo Davidson Trust: 'The Prizes have been awarded annually to young probabilists since 1976'; no numeric age or career-stage limit is published.

typical_recipient: readers and full professors (Schmidt: Bristol; Barker: Cardiff; Annen: Czech Academy senior researcher)
rule_text: Recipient must have completed "no more than 25 years of full-time equivalent research" (historically under 45 years of age), so as to be "not too old for further work, and not too young to have done much".

typical_recipient: lecturers and associate professors (Keating 2021; Ding, Gwynne 2023)
rule_text: LMS prize for 'a definite piece of research actually published by the Society during the eight years ending on 31 December of year X-1' by an author with 'fewer than 15 years (full time equivalent) of involvement in mathematics at post-doctoral level (calculated from the date of award of their PhD)'.

typical_recipient: independent group leaders and assistant/associate professors under 40
rule_text: OeAW: applicants must hold a completed doctorate and be under 40 at application (extended up to four years for childcare), with three years of continuous research in Austria or a partner country.

Award Name: Annie Jump Cannon Award in Astronomy
typical_recipient: late postdocs and newly appointed assistant professors
rule_text: For "outstanding research and promise for future research by a female researcher within five years after earning her PhD".

typical_recipient: full professors (Braverman, Princeton 2022; Oveis Gharan, U Washington 2026)
rule_text: 'A candidate's 40th birthday must not occur before January 1st of the year of the Congress at which the Medal is awarded.'

typical_recipient: assistant professors (one industrial research staff member)
rule_text: IJCAI: 'Nominees for the IJCAI Computers and Thought Award should have received their PhD within the last 7 years at the date of the IJCAI conference', extendable for parenting leave, national service or other exceptional circumstances.

Award Name: Walter L. Huber Civil Engineering Research Prize
typical_recipient: associate professors (a few full professors)
rule_text: ASCE "mid-career research award"; preference to members "generally under 40 years of age".

Award Name: J. H. Wilkinson Prize for Numerical Software
typical_recipient: research scientists and junior faculty (Van Zee, UT Austin and Matthews, SMU 2023; Julia founders 2019)
rule_text: 'Candidates must have worked in mathematics or science for at most 12 years (full time equivalent) after receiving their PhD as of January 1 of the award year', allowing for breaks in continuity; the committee may make exceptions for candidates at an equivalent career stage.

Award Name: Ruth Lyttle Satter Prize in Mathematics
typical_recipient: full professors
rule_text: AMS: for 'an outstanding contribution to mathematics research by a woman in the previous six years'; no age or career-stage restriction.

typical_recipient: full professors (Miller: Cambridge; Ding: Peking; Corwin: Columbia)
rule_text: Recognizes "outstanding contributions by researchers in probability who are under 45 years old".

typical_recipient: tenure-track assistant professors
rule_text: Candidates 'must be tenure-track, though untenured, as of September 15' of the nomination year, hold a PhD and a faculty post with a regular teaching obligation at a US or Canadian institution; no years-since-PhD cap in the current rules (the bulk pilot report records a six-year post-PhD cap for earlier cohorts).

typical_recipient: CNRS chargés de recherche and maîtres de conférences, some postdocs (2-6 years past PhD)
rule_text: Collège de France: the Peccot lectures are entrusted to mathematicians under 30 years of age.

typical_recipient: assistant to full professors and group leaders (Marks, Bock, Dessimoz, Engelhardt, Li)
rule_text: ISCB awards it to "early or mid-career phase scientists" for outstanding accomplishment in computational biology; no age or years-since-PhD cap.

typical_recipient: PhD students (Ilango, MIT 2023; Huang, MIT 2024)
rule_text: Best student paper award at IEEE FOCS, given 'to the author(s) of the best student paper(s)'; a paper qualifies when 'all authors are full-time students at the date of the submission'.

Award Name: Michael Brin Prize in Dynamical Systems
typical_recipient: associate and full professors
rule_text: Awarded to mathematicians who 'have made outstanding advances in the field of dynamical systems and are within 14 years of their PhD' (a separate Brin Prize for Young Mathematicians covers researchers within 4 years of the PhD).

typical_recipient: full professors and CNRS research directors (Norreys: Oxford; Triaud: Birmingham; Claudin and Andreotti: CNRS/ESPCI)
rule_text: IOP/SFP bilateral award "for distinguished work in any aspect of physics that is ongoing or has been carried out within the 10 years preceding the award"; no age or career-stage restriction.

typical_recipient: full professors (LSE, UCL, Mannheim, KU Leuven)
rule_text: 'A European economist under 45 who has made a contribution in theoretical and applied research significant to economics in Europe.'

typical_recipient: tenure-track and newly tenured professors at R1 universities
rule_text: NAS: for 'early-career researchers (preferably 45 years of age or younger)' in experimental psychology; the age cap is a preference, not a hard rule.

Award Name: Leslie Fox Prize for Numerical Analysis
typical_recipient: PhD students and postdocs (Cortinovis: Stanford; Weber: Harvard; Roberts: ANU)
rule_text: Open to "any person who is less than 31 years old" on 1 January of the prize year (career breaks may be allowed for).

typical_recipient: faculty at developing-country institutions (Tagliazucchi, UBA and Laha, TIFR 2024; Jolly, IISc 2023)
rule_text: For 'outstanding and original contributions in physics by young scientists from, and working in, developing countries'; candidates must have obtained their PhD less than 12 years before the award year (extended by one year per child for women).

typical_recipient: associate professors and independent group leaders
rule_text: NAS: for 'young (no older than 45) French and American scientists' in biology and medicine.

typical_recipient: full professors (Hom: Georgia Tech; Greene: Boston College; Bauer: Ljubljana)
rule_text: For "outstanding expository papers published in the Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society or the Notices of the American Mathematical Society in the previous five years"; no age restriction.

typical_recipient: assistant and associate professors (Vogt, Technion 2023; Hoye, Oxford 2024)
rule_text: Joint IOM3/RSC/SCI award for 'work of exceptional practical significance' by an early-career scientist; historically 'nominees should be no older than 39 years of age', and from 2026 IOM3 defines early career as 'within 10 years of the start of their first employment ... or within 6 years of completing their PhD ..., whichever is sooner'.

typical_recipient: tenure-track assistant professors
rule_text: Eurocomb: 'Recipients must not be older than 35'.

typical_recipient: PhD students
rule_text: For "women pursuing Ph.D./doctoral degrees" in aerospace engineering or space sciences, registered full-time and with at least one year of the doctoral program completed; "post-doctoral research programs are not eligible".

typical_recipient: independent group leaders and lecturers to readers, about 7-11 years post-PhD
rule_text: Biochemical Society medal for an early-career biochemist 'within 10 years of receiving their highest qualification' (career breaks extend the window; before 2019 the rule was 'under 35').

typical_recipient: full professors (Stanford GSB, Chicago Booth, Minnesota)
rule_text: For young economists from the European Union: 'Prizewinners are economists under the age of 40'.

typical_recipient: postdocs and junior group leaders (Abad Andrade: Caltech postdoc; Ivleva: TUM group leader; Meermann: BAM division head)
rule_text: GDCh/DAAS prize for "herausragender spektroskopischer Leistungen des reiferen wissenschaftlichen Nachwuchses" (outstanding spectroscopic achievements of advanced junior scientists) from universities, research institutes or industry; no numeric age cap.

typical_recipient: secondary-school pupils
rule_text: 'Open to pre-university young people ages 15-20 who have conducted water-related projects' on topics of environmental, scientific, social or technological importance.

typical_recipient: assistant and associate professors
rule_text: AGU: 'The nominee must be an early career scientist within 10 years of receiving their Ph.D. or highest equivalent terminal degree'.

typical_recipient: PhD students
rule_text: Best student paper at the Physical Electronics Conference: "a paper based on a Ph.D. thesis whose date of submission is no earlier than one year before the meeting"; authors limited to the student and PhD advisor.

typical_recipient: fresh PhDs, usually postdocs at award time
rule_text: 'Ph.D. dissertations concerning a topic in Logic, Language, or Information are eligible for the prize, if the degree was awarded between January 1st and December 31st' of the preceding year; nomination by the supervisor, self-nomination not allowed.

typical_recipient: assistant professors
rule_text: SfAA/AAA: for 'early career scholars (no more than 10 years past receipt of their doctorate)'.

typical_recipient: full professors and HHMI/Janelia investigators (Vosshall: Rockefeller; Jayaraman: Janelia; Maimon: Rockefeller)
rule_text: Given by Columbia's Department of Neuroscience and Kavli Institute "to an investigator in recognition of outstanding research contributions in Neural Science"; no age, career-stage or time-window rule stated (historically described as honouring young investigators).

typical_recipient: full professors (LMU, Bonn, Zurich, Kiel)
rule_text: Verein fuer Socialpolitik prize for an economist from the German-speaking area ('Wirtschaftswissenschaftler aus dem deutschen Sprachraum') under 45 who has gained international recognition through publications in leading journals.

typical_recipient: assistant and associate professors
rule_text: Optica: 'Candidates must be within ten (10) years of the completion of their highest degree earned in the year the medal is presented, excluding career breaks'.

typical_recipient: tenure-track or tenured professors (Colombo: EPFL; Ros-Oton: ICREA/Barcelona; De Philippis: SISSA)
rule_text: Reserved for a mathematician who, "entro la fine dell'anno in cui viene emanato il bando, non abbia compiuto 35 anni" (has not turned 35 by the end of the year of the call).

typical_recipient: independent group leaders (Bharat, MRC LMB and Bikard, Pasteur 2025)
rule_text: Recognises 'remarkable achievements of scientists under the age of 40 in Europe'.

typical_recipient: full professors and senior research scientists
rule_text: EAG: a mid-career award; 'Candidates must have received a recognized doctorate within 25 years of the first day of the year in which the award is given'.

typical_recipient: assistant and associate professors (Cheung: Berkeley; Miller: CMU; Madsen: Aarhus)
rule_text: "No one can be a candidate for the junior prize, if his/her PhD graduation year dates back more than seven years before the year in which the DN junior prize will be awarded" (parental and sick leave excluded).

typical_recipient: fresh PhDs from Max Planck institutes, typically postdocs at award time
rule_text: Max Planck Society medal 'to young researchers for outstanding scientific achievements, mostly in connection with their doctorate' (up to 30 per year across the three MPG sections).

typical_recipient: fresh PhDs from Max Planck institutes, typically postdocs at award time
rule_text: Max Planck Society: awarded 'to young researchers for outstanding scientific achievements, mostly in connection with their doctorate' (a doctoral-dissertation prize).

typical_recipient: fresh PhDs, mostly postdocs at time of award
rule_text: Dissertation prize of the Max Planck Society: "Anyone who has completed his or her doctoral thesis before turning 30 may be put forward", nominated by the MPI director where the doctorate was done.

typical_recipient: assistant professors and staff scientists (Mistlberger, SLAC 2021; Engelhardt, MIT 2023; Eberhardt, Amsterdam 2025)
rule_text: EPS High Energy and Particle Physics Division medal in theoretical particle physics or field theory for a researcher with a 'maximum of 8 years - excluding career interruptions - of research experience following the PhD'.

Award Name: E. H. Moore Research Article Prize
typical_recipient: full professors
rule_text: AMS: for an outstanding research article in one of the AMS primary research journals 'during the previous six years'; no age or career-stage restriction.

typical_recipient: associate and full professors, senior industry researchers (Das: Michigan; Wu: Meta; Krishna: Georgia Tech)
rule_text: For "an outstanding contribution to computer architecture made by an individual whose computer-related professional career (graduate school or full-time employment, whichever began first) started no earlier than January 1st of the year that is 20 years prior to the year of the award".

typical_recipient: PhD students (Ho, MIT 2015; Briden, MIT 2022)
rule_text: IAF award to a young scientist under 30 years of age who has contributed significantly to space science and presented a first-authored paper at the IAC (discontinued after 2022; succeeded by the IAF Young Pioneer Award).

Award Name: LTPP Data Analysis Contest - Challenge Category
typical_recipient: MS/PhD students in civil engineering with faculty advisors as co-authors
rule_text: FHWA/ASCE guidelines: 'A team shall consist of one to four students at any level (undergraduate and/or graduate), external partners if applicable, and may include the faculty advisor as a contributing author'.

typical_recipient: associate professors (Koukoulopoulos: Montreal; Pasten: PUC Chile; Stange: Colorado Boulder)
rule_text: For distinguished research in number theory by a mathematician who is Canadian or has close connections to Canadian mathematics; "Normally, the winner will have received their Ph.D. in the last 12 years".

typical_recipient: full professors (Procaccia, Moulin 2024; Babichenko, Rubinstein 2021)
rule_text: Game Theory Society prize for an article at the interface of game theory and computer science whose 'main results were not published ... 14 or more years before the year of the award'; 'preference will be given to candidates of age 45 or less at the time of the award, but this is not an absolute constraint'.

typical_recipient: assistant professors
rule_text: EATCS: nominees must, by January 1 of the nomination year, be 'at most 35 years old, or having finished their PhD at most 6 years ago' (extensions for leaves per ERC Starting Grant rules).

typical_recipient: full professors (Tisseur: Manchester; Thomas: Imperial; Breuillard: Oxford)
rule_text: LMS regulations: awarded only to a mathematician "who has fewer than 25 years (full time equivalent) of involvement in mathematics at post-doctoral level, allowing for breaks in continuity", or at an equivalent career stage.

typical_recipient: senior full professors (Courcelle 2022; Bodlaender, Fomin et al. 2024)
rule_text: EATCS-IPEC prize 'to a research paper or series of research papers ... published in a recognized refereed journal' in multivariate algorithms and complexity; 'the past restrictions that required a certain number of years before/after the publication of the nominated papers have been removed'; no career-stage restriction.

typical_recipient: PhD students, postdocs and assistant professors
rule_text: Economic History Society: the author must satisfy one of 'The author is within five years of receipt of her/his PhD' or 'The author normally has no previous publication in the field of economic and/or social history'.

typical_recipient: assistant to full professors (Goldberg: Berkeley; Aspero: UEA; Schindler: Munster)
rule_text: European Set Theory Society medal for "the most influential published work in set theory in the last five years"; no age or career-stage restriction.

typical_recipient: assistant and associate professors and staff scientists (Bakr, Princeton and Haah, Stanford 2025)
rule_text: Breakthrough Prize rules: 'targeted toward early-career researchers'; 'there are no age restrictions'; 'candidates ... will generally be no more than 12 years past their PhD', with exceptions for experimental projects with long lead times.

typical_recipient: associate and full professors
rule_text: Breakthrough Prize: for 'early-career researchers who have already produced important work'; 'Candidates for the New Horizons Prize should have not held a PhD for more than 10 years at the start of the calendar year in which nominations close', relaxable in exceptional circumstances.

Award Name: James Clerk Maxwell Medal and Prize
typical_recipient: lecturers and research fellows (Clough: QMUL lecturer; Breuckmann: Bristol lecturer; Schindler: Imperial research fellow)
rule_text: IOP Bronze Early Career medal "for exceptional early-career contributions to theoretical (including mathematical and computational) physics"; IOP early-career awards are for physicists "within six years of their PhD graduation date" (or within ten years of starting physics work without a PhD).
